sample.question:
Tower of Hanoi is a classic puzzle with three pegs labeled A, B and C (left to right) and several disks of different sizes. Disks are numbered by size: disk 1 is the smallest. A disk's number is printed on it. Only the TOP disk of a peg can be moved, and it may only be placed on an empty peg or on top of a LARGER disk. The move X->Y means: take the top disk of peg X and put it on peg Y.

Starting from the position in the image, what is the minimum number of moves needed to gather all 3 disks on peg C (in proper size order)? Answer with a single number.
sample.analysis:
Initial position: peg A: disks [3] (bottom to top); peg B: empty; peg C: disks [2, 1] (bottom to top).
An exhaustive breadth-first search over all reachable positions shows the optimum is 7 moves. One optimal sequence:
Move 1: C->A (disk 1) -> peg A: disks [3, 1] (bottom to top); peg B: empty; peg C: disks [2] (bottom to top).
Move 2: C->B (disk 2) -> peg A: disks [3, 1] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [2] (bottom to top); peg C: empty.
Move 3: A->B (disk 1) -> peg A: disks [3] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [2, 1] (bottom to top); peg C: empty.
Move 4: A->C (disk 3) -> peg A: empty; peg B: disks [2, 1] (bottom to top); peg C: disks [3] (bottom to top).
Move 5: B->A (disk 1) -> peg A: disks [1] (bottom to top); peg B: disks [2] (bottom to top); peg C: disks [3] (bottom to top).
Move 6: B->C (disk 2) -> peg A: disks [1] (bottom to top); peg B: empty; peg C: disks [3, 2] (bottom to top).
Move 7: A->C (disk 1) -> peg A: empty; peg B: empty; peg C: disks [3, 2, 1] (bottom to top).
All disks are now on peg C, and the search guarantees no shorter solution exists.
So the answer is 7.
